name: All Fours (North American)
description: North American All Fours, widely known in the 19th century as Seven Up or Old Sledge, is the classic American iteration of the English game. It introduced the 'Seven point' target and refined the 'Discarding' mechanic when the cards are run, making it a faster and more tactical game than its 17th-century ancestor.

overview.description: North American All Fours, widely known in the 19th century as Seven Up or Old Sledge, is the classic American iteration of the English game. It introduced the 'Seven point' target and refined the 'Discarding' mechanic when the cards are run, making it a faster and more tactical game than its 17th-century ancestor.

history.origins: Brought to America by English settlers, All Fours became the most popular card game in the US before the rise of Poker and Bridge. It was famously played by Abraham Lincoln and documented as the primary 'gambling game' of the frontier.
timeline: 1830s: Seven Up becomes the standard name in American gaming parlors.
1860s: Civil War soldiers popularize the game in military camps.
1900s: Gradually evolves into faster variants like 'Pitch' (Auction Pitch).
history.cultural: Often associated with the 'Old West'. Winning a game of Seven Up was a common theme in period literature and tall tales.
history.evolution: The transition from an 11-point target to a 7-point target (hence 'Seven Up') made the game ideal for quick matches in commercial settings.

setup.dealing: Dealer gives 6 cards to each player (traditionally 3 at a time). The 13th card is turned up for trumps.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, 7 chips per player/team for scoring.

rules.objective: Score 7 points by winning High, Low, Jack, and Game in several hands.
rules.gameplay:
1. **The Turn-Up**: Dealer flips a card for trumps. 2. **The Beg**: Non-dealer (Eldest) can either 'Stand' (accept trump) or 'Beg'. 3. **The Gift/Run**: If they beg, dealer can: 
   - 'Gift' 1 point to the opponent and keep the trump suit.
   - OR 'Run the cards': Deal 3 more cards to each player. Flip a new trump. (If the new suit is the same as the first, keep running 3 at a time until a different suit appears).
4. **Discarding**: If the cards were run, players discard down to exactly 6 cards before play starts. 5. **Play**: Follow suit or trump. 6. **Scoring**: Points awarded in order: High, Low, Jack, Game.
keyRules: High (1 pt): Held by the player dealt the highest trump.
Low (1 pt): Held by the player dealt the lowest trump.
Jack (1 pt): Awarded to the team that WINS the trick containing the Jack of trumps.
Game (1 pt): Awarded to the team with the most 'pips' from captured tricks (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).
Game Tie: If the pip count is tied, the point goes to the non-dealing side (Eldest).

strategy.basic: Always protect your 10s. Since they are worth 10 points for 'Game', losing one can forfeit the Game point entirely.
strategy.intermediate: The Discard: When running the cards and discarding to 6, throw away your low cards in non-trump suits to increase your chances of being 'void' and thus able to trump early.
strategy.advanced: Dealer Strategy: If an opponent begs and you hold the King or Jack of trumps, strongly consider 'Gifting' the 1 point. It's often safer than risking a new trump suit where they might find the Ace.
tips: Low belongs to the holder. If you have the 2 of trumps, it is yours even if you lose that trick.
In 4-player games, leading a small trump can smoke out the opponent's Jack if your partner holds the Ace.

variations.name: Old Sledge
variations.description: The exact same game but historically played to 9 or 11 points in some localized areas.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Historically played to a different target score; engine overrides for scoring variant not modeled yet.

variations.name: Blind All Fours
variations.description: No card is turned; the first card led by the Eldest hand sets the trumps.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Trump is set by the first lead instead of a turn-up; this start-of-hand variant is documented but not encoded as engine overrides yet.

scoring.description: Points are scored in a strict 1-by-1 sequence.
scoring.winCondition: The first side to reach 7 points wins the hand/match.

synthesis.shortDescription: Play the game that captivated Abraham Lincoln and defined early American leisure. A sharp, 7-point battle of wits where you must hunt the Jack and protect your Tens.
